lines.text: A foolish woman tears her house down with her own hands, and a fool's proud speech brings a rod to his back.
An abundant harvest comes through the strength of the ox, and a mocker seeks wisdom but finds none.
No stranger shares the heart's joy, and the house of the wicked will be destroyed while the tent of the upright flourishes.
The poor man is hated even by his brother, but many love the rich, and the one who is kind to the poor is blessed.
Envy rots the bones, and whoever oppresses the poor taunts their Maker, but the righteous man has a refuge even in sleep.
